english.title: Pilot in command fail to ensure all passengers / baggage properly secured
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the pilot in command of an aircraft registered in the United Kingdom, namely **(..SPECIFY AIRCRAFT..), which was on a public transport flight, failed,

(A)_[after the embarkation of its passengers for the purpose of taking off, from the moment when the aircraft first moved until after it had taken off,]_
(B)_[before it landed, until it came to rest for the purpose of the disembarkation of its passengers,]_
(C)_[when, by reason of turbulent air or emergency occurring during the flight you considered it necessary to do so,]_
(D)_[**(..SPECIFY COMBINATION OF THE ABOVE..]_

to take all reasonable steps to ensure that

(E)_[all passengers of two years of age or more were properly secured in their seats by safety belts (with diagonal shoulder strap, if required to be carried) or safety harnesses]_
(F)_[all passengers under the age of two years were properly secured by means of a child restraint device]_
(G)_[those items of baggage in the passenger compartment which you reasonably considered ought by virtue of their size, weight or nature to be properly secured were properly secured]_
(H)_[those items of baggage in the passenger compartment in the case of an aircraft capable of seating more than 30 passengers, were either stowed in the passenger compartment stowage spaces approved by the CAA for the purpose or carried in accordance with the terms of a permission granted by the CAA]_
(I)_[**(..SPECIFY COMBINATION OF THE ABOVE..]_
english.legislation: Contrary to articles 106(4) and 265(6) of the Air Navigation Order 2016.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being the pilot in command of an aircraft registered in the United Kingdom, which was on a public transport flight, failed,
after the embarkation of its passengers for the purpose of taking off, from the moment when the aircraft first moved until after it had taken off,
before it landed, until it came to rest for the purpose of the disembarkation of its passengers and when, by reason of turbulent air or emergency occurring during the flight you considered it necessary to do so,
to take all reasonable steps to ensure that
all passengers of two years of age or more were properly secured in their seats by safety belts (with diagonal shoulder strap, if required to be carried) or safety harnesses,
all passengers under the age of two years were properly secured by means of a child restraint device,
those items of baggage in the passenger compartment which you reasonably considered ought by virtue of their size, weight or nature to be properly secured were properly secured and those items of baggage in the passenger compartment in the case of an aircraft capable of seating more than 30 passengers, were either stowed in the passenger compartment stowage spaces approved by the CAA for the purpose or carried in accordance with the terms of a permission granted by the CAA
